title: Spatio-Temporal model results
text:
# Data
This analysis builds on the tidal features calculated in the previous stages of the analysis. The estimated tidal levels (HAT, MHWS, MHWN, MSL, MLWN, MLWS and LAT) from the individual tide-gauge stations are brought together here to investigate how these features vary across both space and time.
The station-level tidal feature estimates are first explored and prepared for spatial analysis. Spatial and spatio-temporal INLA models are then fitted to each tidal feature, allowing information to be shared between locations and through time. The fitted spatio-temporal models are subsequently used to predict each tidal feature across the Irish coastal domain, providing estimates at locations where tide-gauge observations are not available.
Show code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggridges)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
library(fmesher)
library(sf)
library(stExtremes)
library(viridis)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
## Get all matching files
files <- list.files(path = here::here("rds"), pattern = "^inla-st-data-.*\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)

## Read and combine into a single tibble
da <- map_dfr(files, readRDS)

title: Spatio-Temporal model results
text:
Model fitting
Six candidate INLA models are fitted separately to each tidal feature. The models are designed to progressively introduce a temporal trend, spatial dependence, and spatio-temporal dependence. This allows the analysis to assess whether variation in each tidal feature can be explained by an overall mean and temporal trend alone, or whether explicitly modelling spatial and spatio-temporal structure provides an improved representation of the data.
The six candidate models are:








Model
Structure
Description




m0
Mean only
Baseline model containing only the overall mean tidal level, with no temporal trend or spatial structure.


m1
Mean + trend
Extends the baseline model by including a linear temporal trend, allowing the tidal feature to systematically increase or decrease through time.


m0s
Mean + spatial field
Includes the barrier SPDE spatial field, allowing tidal levels to vary spatially between locations while accounting for the coastline and land barriers. No systematic temporal trend is included.


m1s
Mean + trend + spatial field
Combines a linear temporal trend with the barrier SPDE spatial field, allowing both systematic change through time and spatial variation between locations.


m0st
Mean + spatio-temporal field
Extends the spatial model by allowing the barrier spatial field to evolve through time according to an AR(1) process. This allows spatial patterns in tidal levels to change between consecutive time points.


m1st
Mean + trend + spatio-temporal field
The most complex model, combining a linear temporal trend with a spatial field that evolves through time according to an AR(1) process.



The models can therefore be considered as a progression in complexity. m0 and m1 provide non-spatial reference models, m0s and m1s introduce spatial dependence through the barrier model, and m0st and m1st additionally allow the spatial field to vary through time. Within each pair, the m1 version includes a linear temporal trend, whereas the corresponding m0 version does not.
For the spatial models, the barrier SPDE allows observations at geographically related coastal locations to share information while restricting direct spatial dependence across land. In the spatio-temporal models, an AR(1) temporal structure is applied to the spatial field, allowing the spatial pattern at one time point to be correlated with the spatial pattern at the preceding time point. The strength of this temporal dependence is controlled by the AR(1) correlation parameter, \(\rho\).
Each of the six models is fitted to HAT, MHWS, MHWN, MSL, MLWN, MLWS and LAT.
Following model fitting, grouped cross-validation (GCV) is calculated for each candidate model. These results are considered alongside the other model diagnostics to compare the alternative formulations and assess whether incorporating a temporal trend, spatial dependence and spatio-temporal dependence improves the representation and predictive performance of each tidal feature.


Show code
## Define formulas
fms <- gen_barrier_model_formulas()
fms_levels <- names(fms)
nm <- length(fms)

## Fit missing models without retaining all fitted models in memory
for (i in seq_along(const_levels)) {
  const <- const_levels[i]
  
  for (j in seq_along(fms)) {
    fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-st-FIXED-%s-%s.rds", const, names(fms)[j]))
    
    if (!file.exists(fl)) {
      message("Fitting ", const, " - ", names(fms)[j])
      
      if (j <= 4) {
        mod <- inla_st(formula = fms[[j]], st = FALSE, data = s_inla_data[[i]], stk = stk.s[[i]])
      } else {
        mod <- inla_st(formula = fms[[j]], st = TRUE, data = st_inla_data[[i]], stk = stk.st[[i]])
      }
      
      saveRDS(mod, fl)
      rm(mod)
      gc(verbose = FALSE)
    }
  }
}

## Calculate/load GCV without holding all fitted models in memory
gcv_fl <- here::here("rds", "tide-models-GCV-FIXED.rds")

if (file.exists(gcv_fl)) {
  gcv <- readRDS(gcv_fl)
} else {
  gcv <- vector("list", length(const_levels))
  names(gcv) <- const_levels
  
  for (i in seq_along(const_levels)) {
    const <- const_levels[i]
    message("Calculating GCV for ", const)
    
    gcv_const <- setNames(numeric(length(fms_levels)), fms_levels)
    
    for (j in seq_along(fms_levels)) {
      model_name <- fms_levels[j]
      model_fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-st-FIXED-%s-%s.rds", const, model_name))
      
      message("  GCV: ", const, " - ", model_name)
      
      mod <- readRDS(model_fl)
      cv <- inla.group.cv(mod, num.level.sets = 5, verbose = FALSE)
      gcv_const[j] <- sum(log(cv$cv), na.rm = TRUE) * -1
      
      rm(mod, cv)
      gc(verbose = FALSE)
    }
    
    gcv[[const]] <- gcv_const
    saveRDS(gcv, gcv_fl)
  }
}

load_const_models <- function(const) {
  mods <- map(fms_levels, \(model) {
    fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-st-FIXED-%s-%s.rds", const, model))
    readRDS(fl)
  })
  
  names(mods) <- fms_levels
  mods
}

title: Spatio-Temporal model results
text:
Model predictions
Predictions are generated across the full marine study domain using a regular spatial grid with 2 km spacing. These spatial locations are then replicated across all temporal indices used in the spatio-temporal model, producing a prediction grid covering both space and time.
A projector matrix is constructed to link each prediction location and time point to the spatio-temporal mesh. The prediction grid is then combined with the estimation stack so that the fitted spatio-temporal model can be evaluated at locations where no tide-gauge observations are available.
Predictions are produced separately for each tidal feature using the m1st model, which contains an overall mean, a linear temporal trend, and a barrier spatial field that evolves through time according to an AR(1) process. The previously estimated hyperparameters are held fixed during the prediction fit, allowing the fitted model structure to be projected onto the full prediction grid.
For each tidal feature and each space-time prediction point, the posterior mean and posterior standard deviation are extracted. These provide the estimated tidal level and its associated uncertainty across the Irish coastal domain through time.


Show code
## Prediction points at 2 km spacing
grid_pts <- st_make_grid(area_model, cellsize = 2, what = "centers")
id.grid.in <- unlist(st_contains(area_model, grid_pts))
n.pred <- length(id.grid.in)
grid_pts_inside <- grid_pts[id.grid.in]
pred.coords <- st_coordinates(grid_pts_inside)

## Expand prediction coordinates over time
prediction_year_idx <- sort(unique(db_st_km[[1]]$year_idx))
n_years <- length(prediction_year_idx)

## Expand prediction coordinates over time
prediction_year_idx <- sort(unique(db_st_km[[1]]$year_idx))
n_years <- length(prediction_year_idx)

## Keep X and Y together as coordinate pairs
pred_coord_df <- as.data.frame(pred.coords)
names(pred_coord_df) <- c("X", "Y")

## Expand each spatial location over all temporal indices
expd_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(pred_coord_df, year_idx = prediction_year_idx)

## Check expected size
stopifnot(nrow(expd_grid) ==n.pred * n_years)


## Prediction projector matrix
pred_loc <- as.matrix(expd_grid[,c("X", "Y")])
A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A(
  mesh,
  loc = pred_loc,
  group = expd_grid$year_idx,
  n.group = n_years
)

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(sum(A.pred)), as.numeric(n.pred * n_years))))

## Number of latent spatio-temporal nodes: mesh$n * n_years

## Year lookup
year_lookup <- db_st_km[[1]] |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(year_idx, year_mid) |>
  arrange(year_idx)

## Sequential prediction fitting/extraction
df_pred <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(const_levels))
names(df_pred) <- const_levels

## Model used for predictions
j_pred <- 6

for (i in seq_along(const_levels)) {
  const <- const_levels[i]
  model_name <- fms_levels[j_pred]
  
  ## Fitted m1st model used to provide hyperparameters for prediction
  fit_fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-st-FIXED-%s-%s.rds", const, model_name))
  
  if (!file.exists(fit_fl)) {
    warning(sprintf("Prediction model %s is unavailable for %s. Predictions will be skipped.", model_name, const))
    df_pred[[i]] <- NULL
    next
  }
  
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  fit_model_i <- readRDS(fit_fl)
  
  ## Build prediction stack for this constituent
  stk.pred.i <- inla.stack(
    data = list(y = NA),
    effects = list(
      w.index[[i]],
      data.frame(m = rep(1, nrow(A.pred)), trendc = expd_grid$year_idx - mean(expd_grid$year_idx))
    ),
    A = list(A.pred, 1),
    tag = "pred"
  )
  
  ## Combine estimation + prediction stacks for this constituent
  stack.full.i <- inla.stack(stk.st[[i]], stk.pred.i)
  stack.full.data.i <- inla.stack.data(stack.full.i)
  
  ## Prediction indices
  idx.pred.i <- inla.stack.index(stack.full.i, tag = "pred")$data
  stopifnot(length(idx.pred.i) == nrow(expd_grid))
  
  ## Saved prediction model
  fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-st-PRED-FIXED-%s-%s.rds", const, model_name))
  
  ## Fit or read one prediction model
  if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    cat(sprintf("## ====== Running model prediction for %s: %s ======\n", const, model_name))
    
    pred_model_i <- inla_st(
      formula = fms[[j_pred]],
      st = TRUE,
      data = stack.full.data.i,
      stk = stack.full.i,
      control.mode = list(theta = unname(fit_model_i$misc$theta.mode), fixed = TRUE)
    )
    
    saveRDS(pred_model_i, fl)
  } else {
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
    pred_model_i <- readRDS(fl)
  }
  
  ## Extract prediction summary
  fitted_summary_i <- pred_model_i$summary.fitted.values
  pred_mean_i <- fitted_summary_i[idx.pred.i, "mean", drop = TRUE]
  pred_sd_i <- fitted_summary_i[idx.pred.i, "sd", drop = TRUE]
  
  stopifnot(length(pred_mean_i) == nrow(expd_grid), length(pred_sd_i) == nrow(expd_grid))
  
  ## Store compact prediction results
  df_pred[[i]] <- tibble(
    lon = expd_grid$X,
    lat = expd_grid$Y,
    year_idx = expd_grid$year_idx,
    mean = pred_mean_i,
    sd = pred_sd_i
  ) |>
    left_join(year_lookup, by = "year_idx")
  
  ## Remove large objects before moving to the next constituent
  rm(fit_model_i, pred_model_i, fitted_summary_i, pred_mean_i, pred_sd_i, stk.pred.i, stack.full.i, stack.full.data.i, idx.pred.i)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

title: Temporal modelling for WexfordHarbour
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at WexfordHarbour.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for WexfordHarbour
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

title: Temporal modelling for UnionHallHarbor
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at UnionHallHarbor.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for UnionHallHarbor
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. title: Temporal modelling for Sligo
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at Sligo.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",

                "============================================================\n\n",

                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,

title: Temporal modelling for RingaskiddyNMCI
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at RingaskiddyNMCI.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)

title: Temporal modelling for PopesQuay
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at PopesQuay.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for PopesQuay
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

title: Temporal modelling for MalinHead-PortmorePier
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at MalinHead-PortmorePier.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for MalinHead-PortmorePier
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

title: Temporal modelling for KilrushLough
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at KilrushLough.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for KilrushLough
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.

title: Temporal modelling for Kenmare
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at Kenmare.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.

MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.

names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Fit models

    for (const in const_levels) {

        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    saveRDS(res, fl)

    res <- readRDS(fl)

title: Temporal modelling for GalwayPort
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at GalwayPort.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for GalwayPort
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.
