Tidal levels (or features) are defined as:

HAT (Highest Astronomical Tide) = maximum predicted astronomical tide over the reference prediction period
MSL (Mean Sea Level) = mean of the time series (or the constant/mean term in the model)
MHWS (Mean High Water Springs) = MSL + M2_amp + S2_amp
MHWN (Mean High Water Neaps) = MSL + M2_amp - S2_amp
MLWN (Mean Low Water Neaps) = MSL - M2_amp + S2_amp
MLWS (Mean Low Water Springs) = MSL - M2_amp - S2_amp
LAT (Lowest Astronomical Tide) = minimum predicted astronomical tide over the reference prediction period

Where:

M2 = principal lunar semi-diurnal (largest constituent)
S2 = principal solar semi-diurnal

Springs occur when M2 and S2 are in phase (add together), creating the highest highs and lowest lows.
Neaps occur when M2 and S2 are out of phase (subtract), creating smaller tidal ranges.


Code
hat_lat_data <- imap_dfr(res, function(window_list, window_name) {
    imap_dfr(window_list, function(fit, year_range) {
        lat_hat_file <- here::here("rds", "lat-hat", sprintf("lat-hat-%s-%s-%s.rds", window_name, year_range, st_id))
        ## Default: no calculation failure
        lat_hat_error <- NA_character_

        ## Read existing result or calculate a new one

        if (file.exists(lat_hat_file)) {
            lat_hat <- readRDS(lat_hat_file)
        } else {
            lat_hat <- tryCatch(calculate_lat_hat(fit = fit), error = function(e) {
                    lat_hat_error <<- conditionMessage(e)
                    cat(sprintf(paste0("WARNING: LAT/HAT calculation failed for ", "%s | %s | %s\n", "Reason: %s\n"),
                            st_id, window_name, year_range, lat_hat_error))

                    tibble(constituent = c("LAT", "HAT"), value = c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
                }
            )
        }

        
        ## Check HAT/LAT values
        ##
        ## This is deliberately a very generous threshold. It is intended only
        ## to identify catastrophic numerical/extrapolation failures such as
        ## HAT/LAT values of hundreds or millions of metres.
        ##
        ## It should not affect plausible tidal estimates.

        MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL <- 20
        lat_value <- lat_hat |>
            filter(constituent == "LAT") |>
            pull(value)
        hat_value <- lat_hat |>
            filter(constituent == "HAT") |>
            pull(value)
        
        ## Determine whether the calculated values are numerically plausible
        invalid_lat_hat <- FALSE
        if (length(lat_value) != 1L || length(hat_value) != 1L) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- paste0("LAT/HAT calculation returned an unexpected number of values.")

        } else if (!is.finite(lat_value) || !is.finite(hat_value)) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- paste0("LAT/HAT calculation returned non-finite values.")

        } else if (abs(lat_value) > MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL || abs(hat_value) > MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- sprintf(paste0("Numerically implausible LAT/HAT values detected ", "(LAT = %.3f m, HAT = %.3f m)."),  lat_value, hat_value)

        } else if (lat_value >= hat_value) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- sprintf(paste0("Invalid LAT/HAT ordering ", "(LAT = %.3f m, HAT = %.3f m)."), lat_value, hat_value)
        }

        ## If the LAT/HAT values are invalid, replace them with NA
        ## The tidal harmonic fit itself is retained. Only the unreliable
        ## astronomical extremes are removed.
        if (invalid_lat_hat) {
            cat(sprintf(paste0("WARNING: Rejecting LAT/HAT for ", "%s | %s | %s\n", "Reason: %s\n"),
                    st_id, window_name, year_range, lat_hat_error))
            lat_hat <- lat_hat |>
                mutate(value = NA_real_)

        } else {
            ## Save only valid LAT/HAT calculations
            if (!file.exists(lat_hat_file)) {
                saveRDS(lat_hat, lat_hat_file)
            }
        }
        
        ## Format output
        lat_hat |>
            select(constituent, value) |>
            mutate(window_size = window_name, year_range = year_range, lat_hat_error = lat_hat_error, .before = 1)
    })
}) |>
    mutate(n_years = as.integer(str_extract(window_size, "\\d+")),
        year_end = as.integer(str_extract(year_range, "(?<=y)\\d+")),
        year_start = as.integer(str_extract(year_range,"\\d+$")),
        year_mid = (year_start + year_end) / 2,
        
        ##  Skerries exclusion
        value = if_else(
            params$station == "SkerriesHarbour" &
                window_size == "y_3" &
                year_start == 2010L &
                year_end == 2012L,
            NA_real_,
            value),
        
        ##  Inishmore exclusion
        value = if_else(
            params$station == "Inishmore" &
                window_size == "y_3" &
                year_start == 2015L &
                year_end == 2017L,
            NA_real_,
            value
        ),

        ## Record why values are missing
        exclusion_reason = case_when(
            params$station == "SkerriesHarbour" &
                window_size == "y_3" &
                year_start == 2010L &
                year_end == 2012L ~ "Insufficient observations in the 2010-2012 rolling window",

            !is.na(lat_hat_error) ~  paste0( "HAT/LAT excluded: ", lat_hat_error),TRUE ~NA_character_))

features1_data <- map(res, \(x) map(x, \(y) y$features1)) |>
    imap_dfr(function(window_list, window_name) {
        imap_dfr(window_list, function(features1_mat, year_range) {

        ## Extract years

        year_start = as.integer(str_extract(year_range, "\\d+$")),
        year_mid = (year_start + year_end) / 2,
        constituent = factor(constituent, levels = c("MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS")),

        ## Values outside +/- 8 m are treated as failed harmonic estimates.
        implausible_value = !is.na(value) & abs(value) > 8,

        ## Remove unreliable values
        value = case_when(
            ## Keep existing Skerries exclusion
            params$station == "SkerriesHarbour" &
                window_size == "y_3" &
                year_start == 2010L &
                year_end == 2012L ~
                NA_real_,

            ## General plausibility filter
            implausible_value ~ NA_real_, TRUE ~ value),

        
        ## Record reason for exclusion
        exclusion_reason = case_when(
            params$station == "SkerriesHarbour" &
                window_size == "y_3" &
                year_start == 2010L &
                year_end == 2012L ~
                "Insufficient observations in the 2010-2012 rolling window",

            implausible_value ~  "Implausible tidal-level estimate outside +/- 6 m", TRUE ~  NA_character_))

## Add HAT and LAT to the existing tidal features
features1_data <- bind_rows(features1_data, hat_lat_data) |>

title: Calculating tidal levels for YoughalQuay
text:
The aim of this document is to explore tide-level data from the Marine Institute (MI) and the Office of Public Works (OPW). The final result should be to obtain the tidal levels for each station in Ireland where MI/OPW has available data.





Code

## Full dataset

## Station-specific start dates

  "Inishmore" = "2016-01-01",

)

## Filter for station

  mutate(year = year(time), .before = "station_id") |>

record_years <- record_days / 365.25

## Minimum record length used in the tidal analysis
MIN_RECORD_YEARS <- 3

## This is the sampling time, completed and standardised to 10 minutes
db_comp <- db |>
    select(-c(year, dtime)) |>
    mutate(time_rounded = floor_date(time, "10 min")) |>
    complete(time_rounded = seq(min(time_rounded), max(time_rounded), by = "10 min")) |>
    group_by(time_rounded) |>
    summarise(
        sea_level = mean(sea_level, na.rm = TRUE),
        n_obs = n(),
        n_na = sum(is.na(sea_level)),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    rename(time = time_rounded) |>
    distinct(time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(time) |>
    mutate(
        sea_level = ifelse(is.nan(sea_level), NA_real_, sea_level),
        dtime = as.numeric(difftime(time, lag(time), units = "mins"))
    )

## Define the period to use for the tidal analysis
##
## Stations must have at least 3 years of data to be included.
## Stations with less than 3 years are excluded.

if (record_years < 3) {
    stop(sprintf("%s has only %.2f years of data and is excluded from the tidal analysis.", st_id, record_years))
}

## Identify complete calendar years

complete_years <- db_comp |>
    mutate(year = year(time), month = month(time)) |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(
        min_month = min(month),

        n_months = n_distinct(month),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    filter(min_month == 1, max_month == 12, n_months == 12) |>
    arrange(year)

## Check that at least one complete calendar year exists
if (nrow(complete_years) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("%s has no complete calendar years available for tidal analysis.", st_id))
}

## First and last complete calendar years
year_first <- min(complete_years$year)
year_last <- max(complete_years$year)
year_all <- year_first:year_last



## Check that the complete-year analysis period contains at least 3 years

if (length(year_all) < 3) {
    stop(sprintf(paste0("%s has %.2f years of raw data, but fewer than 3 complete ", "calendar years are available after restricting the analysis period."), st_id, record_years))
}



## Restrict to complete-year period
db_comp <- db_comp |>
    filter(year(time) >= year_first, year(time) <= year_last) |>
    arrange(time)

dtab_comp <- db_comp |>
    summarise(dmin = min(time), dmax = max(time))


To standardise the sample interval, a sampling interval is defined, and all the data was adjuted to fit between this interval.
This was determined using the first and last “full years” of the dataset, i.e., the first and final years where data is available for all the 12 months. In this case, the first full year is 2020, and the last full year is 2024, giving in total a range of 5 years.

## Create rolling windows

names(seq) <- sprintf("y_%s", k)



## Name individual year windows
for (i in seq_along(seq)) {

## Check that each proposed window contains usable observations
## Some stations may span several calendar years but contain little or no
## usable sea-level data within an individual rolling window. Remove such
## windows before fitting the TideHarmonics model.

seq_checked <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(seq))
names(seq_checked) <- names(seq)


for (i in seq_along(seq)) {
    valid_windows <- list()
    for (j in seq_along(seq[[i]])) {
        n1 <- names(seq)[[i]]
        n2 <- names(seq[[i]])[[j]]
        
        ## Define calendar-year limits for this window
        t1 <- make_datetime(year = min(seq[[i]][[j]]))
        t2 <- make_datetime(year = max(seq[[i]][[j]]), month = 12, day = 31, hour = 23, min = 50)
        
        ## Extract data for this window
        db_window <- db_comp |>
            filter(time >= t1, time <= t2)
        
        ## Count usable sea-level observations
        n_non_na <- sum(!is.na(db_window$sea_level))

        ## Keep only windows containing usable observations
        if (n_non_na > 0) {
            valid_windows[[n2]] <- seq[[i]][[j]]
        } 
    }

    ## Store valid windows for this window size
    seq_checked[[i]] <- valid_windows
}



## Remove window-size groups containing no valid windows
seq <- seq_checked[lengths(seq_checked) > 0]


## Stop if no usable windows remain
if (length(seq) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("No usable tidal-analysis windows remain for station %s.", st_id))
}

## Create a list to hold model results
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(seq))
names(res) <- names(seq)


for (i in seq_along(res)) {
    res[[i]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(seq[[i]]))
    names(res[[i]]) <- names(seq[[i]])
}



## Fit all valid windows
for (i in seq_along(res)) {
    for (j in seq_along(res[[i]])) {

        n1 <- names(seq)[[i]]
        n2 <- names(seq[[i]])[[j]]
        
        ## Define calendar-year limits
        t1 <- make_datetime(year = min(seq[[i]][[j]]))
        t2 <- make_datetime(year = max(seq[[i]][[j]]), month = 12, day = 31, hour = 23, min = 50)

        ## Extract data for this fitting window
        db_window <- db_comp |>
            filter(time >= t1, time <= t2)
        
        ## Model file
        fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("fit-%s-%s-%s.rds", n1, n2, st_id))

        ## Fit model if it has not already been saved
        if (!file.exists(fl)) {
            res[[i]][[j]] <- fit_th(x = db_window$sea_level, dto = db_window$time, pred = FALSE)
            saveRDS(res[[i]][[j]], fl)

        } else {
           res[[i]][[j]] <- readRDS(fl)
        }
    }
}


The harmonic model was fitted for three different time intervals (or time windows):

3 years
5 years
NA years.






K1, O1, M2, and S2 are the main tidal constituents because they represent the dominant astronomical forcing mechanisms and typically have the largest amplitudes.

Semi-diurnal constituents (2 cycles per day):

M2 (Principal lunar semi-diurnal): The largest tidal constituent in most places. Period = 12.42 hours. Caused by the moon’s gravitational pull as Earth rotates beneath it.
S2 (Principal solar semi-diurnal): Second largest semi-diurnal constituent. Period = 12.00 hours. Caused by the sun’s gravitational pull.

Diurnal constituents (1 cycle per day):

K1 (Lunisolar diurnal): Largest diurnal constituent. Period = 23.93 hours. Results from the declination of the moon and sun.
O1 (Principal lunar diurnal): Second largest diurnal constituent. Period = 25.82 hours. Due to lunar declination effects.


Why these four matters:

Largest amplitudes: They typically account for 70-90% of tidal variance
Physical significance:

M2 & S2 create spring-neap cycles (14-day variation)
K1 & O1 create diurnal inequality (different heights of successive high/low tides)

Tidal classification: The form factor (K1+O1)/(M2+S2) uses these to classify whether tides are semi-diurnal, diurnal, or mixed
Coastal features: MHWS, MLWS, etc. are primarily defined by M2 and S2



Code
## Extract constituent amplitudes
constituent_amps <- map(res, \(x) map(x, \(y) {
  coefs <- y$coefficients
  tibble(
    K1 = sqrt(coefs["K1_C"]^2 + coefs["K1_S"]^2),
    O1 = sqrt(coefs["O1_C"]^2 + coefs["O1_S"]^2),
    M2 = sqrt(coefs["M2_C"]^2 + coefs["M2_S"]^2),
    S2 = sqrt(coefs["S2_C"]^2 + coefs["S2_S"]^2)
  )
})) |>
  imap_dfr(function(window_list, window_name) {
    imap_dfr(window_list, function(amps, year_range) {
      amps |>
        mutate(window_size = window_name, year_range = year_range, .before = 1)
    })
  }) |>
  mutate(
    n_years = as.integer(str_extract(window_size, "\\d+")),
    year_end = as.integer(str_extract(year_range, "(?<=y)\\d+")),
    year_start = as.integer(str_extract(year_range, "\\d+$")),
    year_mid = (year_start + year_end) / 2
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(K1, O1, M2, S2), names_to = "constituent", values_to = "amplitude")

## Plot
## Extract the last window size as the full-record reference
ly <- constituent_amps$window_size |> tail(1)

amps_ref <- constituent_amps |>
    filter(window_size == ly) |>
    select(constituent, amplitude)

## Create better labels for window_size

The form factor is calculated by
\[(K1+O1)/(M2+S2)\]
and it classifies tides as:

< 0.25: Semi-diurnal
0.25-1.5: Mixed, mainly semi-diurnal
1.5-3.0: Mixed, mainly diurnal
> 3.0: Diurnal

Tidal levels (or features) are defined as:

HAT (Highest Astronomical Tide) = maximum predicted astronomical tide over the reference prediction period
MSL (Mean Sea Level) = mean of the time series (or the constant/mean term in the model)
MHWS (Mean High Water Springs) = MSL + M2_amp + S2_amp
MHWN (Mean High Water Neaps) = MSL + M2_amp - S2_amp
MLWN (Mean Low Water Neaps) = MSL - M2_amp + S2_amp
MLWS (Mean Low Water Springs) = MSL - M2_amp - S2_amp
LAT (Lowest Astronomical Tide) = minimum predicted astronomical tide over the reference prediction period

Where:

M2 = principal lunar semi-diurnal (largest constituent)
S2 = principal solar semi-diurnal

Springs occur when M2 and S2 are in phase (add together), creating the highest highs and lowest lows.
Neaps occur when M2 and S2 are out of phase (subtract), creating smaller tidal ranges.

hat_lat_data <- imap_dfr(res, function(window_list, window_name) {
    imap_dfr(window_list, function(fit, year_range) {
        lat_hat_file <- here::here("rds", "lat-hat", sprintf("lat-hat-%s-%s-%s.rds", window_name, year_range, st_id))
        ## Default: no calculation failure
        lat_hat_error <- NA_character_

        ## Read existing result or calculate a new one

        if (file.exists(lat_hat_file)) {
            lat_hat <- readRDS(lat_hat_file)
        } else {
            lat_hat <- tryCatch(calculate_lat_hat(fit = fit), error = function(e) {
                    lat_hat_error <<- conditionMessage(e)
                    cat(sprintf(paste0("WARNING: LAT/HAT calculation failed for ", "%s | %s | %s\n", "Reason: %s\n"),
                            st_id, window_name, year_range, lat_hat_error))

                    tibble(constituent = c("LAT", "HAT"), value = c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
                }
            )
        }

        
        ## Check HAT/LAT values
        ##
        ## This is deliberately a very generous threshold. It is intended only
        ## to identify catastrophic numerical/extrapolation failures such as
        ## HAT/LAT values of hundreds or millions of metres.
        ##
        ## It should not affect plausible tidal estimates.

        MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL <- 20
        lat_value <- lat_hat |>
            filter(constituent == "LAT") |>
            pull(value)
        hat_value <- lat_hat |>
            filter(constituent == "HAT") |>
            pull(value)
        
        ## Determine whether the calculated values are numerically plausible
        invalid_lat_hat <- FALSE
        if (length(lat_value) != 1L || length(hat_value) != 1L) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- paste0("LAT/HAT calculation returned an unexpected number of values.")

        } else if (!is.finite(lat_value) || !is.finite(hat_value)) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- paste0("LAT/HAT calculation returned non-finite values.")

        } else if (abs(lat_value) > MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL || abs(hat_value) > MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- sprintf(paste0("Numerically implausible LAT/HAT values detected ", "(LAT = %.3f m, HAT = %.3f m)."),  lat_value, hat_value)

        } else if (lat_value >= hat_value) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- sprintf(paste0("Invalid LAT/HAT ordering ", "(LAT = %.3f m, HAT = %.3f m)."), lat_value, hat_value)
        }

        ## If the LAT/HAT values are invalid, replace them with NA
        ## The tidal harmonic fit itself is retained. Only the unreliable
        ## astronomical extremes are removed.
        if (invalid_lat_hat) {
            cat(sprintf(paste0("WARNING: Rejecting LAT/HAT for ", "%s | %s | %s\n", "Reason: %s\n"),
                    st_id, window_name, year_range, lat_hat_error))
            lat_hat <- lat_hat |>
                mutate(value = NA_real_)

        } else {
            ## Save only valid LAT/HAT calculations
            if (!file.exists(lat_hat_file)) {
                saveRDS(lat_hat, lat_hat_file)
            }
        }
        
        ## Format output
        lat_hat |>
            select(constituent, value) |>
            mutate(window_size = window_name, year_range = year_range, lat_hat_error = lat_hat_error, .before = 1)
    })
}) |>

title: Calculating tidal levels for YoughalQuay
text: The aim of this document is to explore tide-level data from the Marine Institute (MI) and the Office of Public Works (OPW). The final result should be to obtain the tidal levels for each station in Ireland where MI/OPW has available data.

title: Calculating tidal levels for YoughalQuay

## Packages
library(arrow)

  "Inishmore" = "2016-01-01",

  "SkerriesHarbour" = "2013-01-01"

## Filter for station

  filter(st_id == params$station) |>
  mutate(year = year(time), .before = "station_id") |>
  mutate(QC_Flag = NULL, sea_level = Water_Level_OD_Malin, Water_Level_OD_Malin = NULL) |>

## Save lat/lon for posterior use

lon <- unique(db$longitude)

record_days <- as.numeric(difftime(record_end, record_start, units = "days"))

record_years <- record_days / 365.25

## This is the sampling time, completed and standardised to 10 minutes
db_comp <- db |>
    select(-c(year, dtime)) |>
    mutate(time_rounded = floor_date(time, "10 min")) |>
    complete(time_rounded = seq(min(time_rounded), max(time_rounded), by = "10 min")) |>
    group_by(time_rounded) |>
    summarise(
        sea_level = mean(sea_level, na.rm = TRUE),
        n_obs = n(),
        n_na = sum(is.na(sea_level)),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    rename(time = time_rounded) |>
    distinct(time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(time) |>
    mutate(
        sea_level = ifelse(is.nan(sea_level), NA_real_, sea_level),
        dtime = as.numeric(difftime(time, lag(time), units = "mins"))
    )

## Define the period to use for the tidal analysis
##
## Stations must have at least 3 years of data to be included.
## Stations with less than 3 years are excluded.

if (record_years < 3) {
    stop(sprintf("%s has only %.2f years of data and is excluded from the tidal analysis.", st_id, record_years))
}

## Identify complete calendar years

complete_years <- db_comp |>
    mutate(year = year(time), month = month(time)) |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(
        min_month = min(month),
        max_month = max(month),
        n_months = n_distinct(month),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    filter(min_month == 1, max_month == 12, n_months == 12) |>
    arrange(year)

## Check that at least one complete calendar year exists
if (nrow(complete_years) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("%s has no complete calendar years available for tidal analysis.", st_id))
}

## First and last complete calendar years
year_first <- min(complete_years$year)
year_last <- max(complete_years$year)
year_all <- year_first:year_last



## Check that the complete-year analysis period contains at least 3 years

if (length(year_all) < 3) {
    stop(sprintf(paste0("%s has %.2f years of raw data, but fewer than 3 complete ", "calendar years are available after restricting the analysis period."), st_id, record_years))
}



## Restrict to complete-year period
db_comp <- db_comp |>
    filter(year(time) >= year_first, year(time) <= year_last) |>
    arrange(time)

dtab_comp <- db_comp |>
    summarise(dmin = min(time), dmax = max(time))


To standardise the sample interval, a sampling interval is defined, and all the data was adjuted to fit between this interval.
This was determined using the first and last “full years” of the dataset, i.e., the first and final years where data is available for all the 12 months. In this case, the first full year is 2020, and the last full year is 2024, giving in total a range of 5 years.
The final dataset has then 262951 observations, within a 10 minute sample interval:

The first observation is on 2020-01-01
The last observation is on 2024-12-31 01:00:00

## Create the fitting windows
k <- c(3, 5, length(year_all))

## Avoid duplicate intervals
##
## For example, if there are exactly 5 years available then:
## 5-year window == full-record window so only one copy is retained.
k <- unique(k)

## Create rolling windows
seq <- map(k, \(x) seq_win(year_all, k = x, step = 1))

names(seq) <- sprintf("y_%s", k)



## Name individual year windows
for (i in seq_along(seq)) {

    names(seq[[i]]) <- sprintf("y%s_%s", sapply(seq[[i]], \(x) max(x)), sapply(seq[[i]], \(x) min(x)))
}



## Display fitting windows as a tidy table

window_table <- imap_dfr(seq, \(window_list, window_name) {
        imap_dfr(window_list, \(years, window_id) {
                tibble(
                    window_size = window_name,
                    year_range = window_id,
                    first_year = min(years),
                    last_year = max(years),
                    n_years = length(years))
            }
        )
    }
)

## Check that each proposed window contains usable observations
## Some stations may span several calendar years but contain little or no
## usable sea-level data within an individual rolling window. Remove such
## windows before fitting the TideHarmonics model.

seq_checked <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(seq))
names(seq_checked) <- names(seq)


for (i in seq_along(seq)) {
    valid_windows <- list()
    for (j in seq_along(seq[[i]])) {
        n1 <- names(seq)[[i]]
        n2 <- names(seq[[i]])[[j]]
        
        ## Define calendar-year limits for this window
        t1 <- make_datetime(year = min(seq[[i]][[j]]))
        t2 <- make_datetime(year = max(seq[[i]][[j]]), month = 12, day = 31, hour = 23, min = 50)
        
        ## Extract data for this window
        db_window <- db_comp |>
            filter(time >= t1, time <= t2)
        
        ## Count usable sea-level observations
        n_non_na <- sum(!is.na(db_window$sea_level))

        ## Keep only windows containing usable observations
        if (n_non_na > 0) {
            valid_windows[[n2]] <- seq[[i]][[j]]
        } 
    }

    ## Store valid windows for this window size
    seq_checked[[i]] <- valid_windows
}



## Remove window-size groups containing no valid windows
seq <- seq_checked[lengths(seq_checked) > 0]


## Stop if no usable windows remain
if (length(seq) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("No usable tidal-analysis windows remain for station %s.", st_id))
}

## Create a list to hold model results
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(seq))
names(res) <- names(seq)


for (i in seq_along(res)) {
    res[[i]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(seq[[i]]))
    names(res[[i]]) <- names(seq[[i]])
}



## Fit all valid windows
for (i in seq_along(res)) {
    for (j in seq_along(res[[i]])) {

        n1 <- names(seq)[[i]]
        n2 <- names(seq[[i]])[[j]]
        
        ## Define calendar-year limits
        t1 <- make_datetime(year = min(seq[[i]][[j]]))
        t2 <- make_datetime(year = max(seq[[i]][[j]]), month = 12, day = 31, hour = 23, min = 50)

        ## Extract data for this fitting window
        db_window <- db_comp |>
            filter(time >= t1, time <= t2)
        
        ## Model file
        fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("fit-%s-%s-%s.rds", n1, n2, st_id))

        ## Fit model if it has not already been saved
        if (!file.exists(fl)) {
            res[[i]][[j]] <- fit_th(x = db_window$sea_level, dto = db_window$time, pred = FALSE)
            saveRDS(res[[i]][[j]], fl)

        } else {
           res[[i]][[j]] <- readRDS(fl)
        }
    }
}


The harmonic model was fitted for three different time intervals (or time windows):

3 years
5 years
NA years.






K1, O1, M2, and S2 are the main tidal constituents because they represent the dominant astronomical forcing mechanisms and typically have the largest amplitudes.

Semi-diurnal constituents (2 cycles per day):

M2 (Principal lunar semi-diurnal): The largest tidal constituent in most places. Period = 12.42 hours. Caused by the moon’s gravitational pull as Earth rotates beneath it.
S2 (Principal solar semi-diurnal): Second largest semi-diurnal constituent. Period = 12.00 hours. Caused by the sun’s gravitational pull.

Diurnal constituents (1 cycle per day):

K1 (Lunisolar diurnal): Largest diurnal constituent. Period = 23.93 hours. Results from the declination of the moon and sun.
O1 (Principal lunar diurnal): Second largest diurnal constituent. Period = 25.82 hours. Due to lunar declination effects.


Why these four matters:

Largest amplitudes: They typically account for 70-90% of tidal variance
Physical significance:

M2 & S2 create spring-neap cycles (14-day variation)
K1 & O1 create diurnal inequality (different heights of successive high/low tides)

Tidal classification: The form factor (K1+O1)/(M2+S2) uses these to classify whether tides are semi-diurnal, diurnal, or mixed
Coastal features: MHWS, MLWS, etc. are primarily defined by M2 and S2

Tidal levels (or features) are defined as:

HAT (Highest Astronomical Tide) = maximum predicted astronomical tide over the reference prediction period
MSL (Mean Sea Level) = mean of the time series (or the constant/mean term in the model)
MHWS (Mean High Water Springs) = MSL + M2_amp + S2_amp
MHWN (Mean High Water Neaps) = MSL + M2_amp - S2_amp
MLWN (Mean Low Water Neaps) = MSL - M2_amp + S2_amp
MLWS (Mean Low Water Springs) = MSL - M2_amp - S2_amp
LAT (Lowest Astronomical Tide) = minimum predicted astronomical tide over the reference prediction period

Where:

M2 = principal lunar semi-diurnal (largest constituent)
S2 = principal solar semi-diurnal

Springs occur when M2 and S2 are in phase (add together), creating the highest highs and lowest lows.
Neaps occur when M2 and S2 are out of phase (subtract), creating smaller tidal ranges.

hat_lat_data <- imap_dfr(res, function(window_list, window_name) {
    imap_dfr(window_list, function(fit, year_range) {
        lat_hat_file <- here::here("rds", "lat-hat", sprintf("lat-hat-%s-%s-%s.rds", window_name, year_range, st_id))
        ## Default: no calculation failure
        lat_hat_error <- NA_character_

        ## Read existing result or calculate a new one

        if (file.exists(lat_hat_file)) {
            lat_hat <- readRDS(lat_hat_file)
        } else {
            lat_hat <- tryCatch(calculate_lat_hat(fit = fit), error = function(e) {
                    lat_hat_error <<- conditionMessage(e)
                    cat(sprintf(paste0("WARNING: LAT/HAT calculation failed for ", "%s | %s | %s\n", "Reason: %s\n"),
                            st_id, window_name, year_range, lat_hat_error))

                    tibble(constituent = c("LAT", "HAT"), value = c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
                }
            )
        }

        
        ## Check HAT/LAT values
        ##
        ## This is deliberately a very generous threshold. It is intended only
        ## to identify catastrophic numerical/extrapolation failures such as
        ## HAT/LAT values of hundreds or millions of metres.
        ##
        ## It should not affect plausible tidal estimates.

        MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL <- 20
        lat_value <- lat_hat |>
            filter(constituent == "LAT") |>
            pull(value)
        hat_value <- lat_hat |>
            filter(constituent == "HAT") |>
            pull(value)
        
        ## Determine whether the calculated values are numerically plausible
        invalid_lat_hat <- FALSE
        if (length(lat_value) != 1L || length(hat_value) != 1L) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- paste0("LAT/HAT calculation returned an unexpected number of values.")

        } else if (!is.finite(lat_value) || !is.finite(hat_value)) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- paste0("LAT/HAT calculation returned non-finite values.")

        } else if (abs(lat_value) > MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL || abs(hat_value) > MAX_ABS_TIDAL_LEVEL) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- sprintf(paste0("Numerically implausible LAT/HAT values detected ", "(LAT = %.3f m, HAT = %.3f m)."),  lat_value, hat_value)

        } else if (lat_value >= hat_value) {
            invalid_lat_hat <- TRUE
            lat_hat_error <- sprintf(paste0("Invalid LAT/HAT ordering ", "(LAT = %.3f m, HAT = %.3f m)."), lat_value, hat_value)
        }

        ## If the LAT/HAT values are invalid, replace them with NA
        ## The tidal harmonic fit itself is retained. Only the unreliable
        ## astronomical extremes are removed.
        if (invalid_lat_hat) {
            cat(sprintf(paste0("WARNING: Rejecting LAT/HAT for ", "%s | %s | %s\n", "Reason: %s\n"),
                    st_id, window_name, year_range, lat_hat_error))
            lat_hat <- lat_hat |>
                mutate(value = NA_real_)

        } else {
            ## Save only valid LAT/HAT calculations
            if (!file.exists(lat_hat_file)) {
                saveRDS(lat_hat, lat_hat_file)
            }
        }
        
        ## Format output
        lat_hat |>
            select(constituent, value) |>
            mutate(window_size = window_name, year_range = year_range, lat_hat_error = lat_hat_error, .before = 1)
    })

title: Temporal modelling for AranmoreIsland-Leabgarrow
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at AranmoreIsland-Leabgarrow.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for AranmoreIsland-Leabgarrow
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

  transmute(constituent, n_obs, n_unique,
    temporal_models_fitted = purrr::map_lgl(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      !is.null(models) && length(models) > 0
    }),
    n_models_fitted = purrr::map_int(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) 0L else length(models)
    }),
    fitted_models = purrr::map_chr(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        stringr::str_extract(names(models), "^m\\d+") |>
          paste(collapse = ", ")
      }
    })) |>
  rename(
    `Tidal feature` = constituent,
    `Observations` = n_obs,
    `Unique values` = n_unique,
    `Models fitted` = temporal_models_fitted,
    `Number fitted` = n_models_fitted,
    `Fitted model set` = fitted_models
  )

title: Temporal modelling for BallyglassHarbour
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at BallyglassHarbour.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for BallyglassHarbour
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

title: Temporal modelling for CarrigaholtPier
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at CarrigaholtPier.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for CarrigaholtPier
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

## Show what was fitted
## Show what was fitted
model_fit_status <- temporal_data_check |>
  transmute(constituent, n_obs, n_unique,
    temporal_models_fitted = purrr::map_lgl(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      !is.null(models) && length(models) > 0
    }),
    n_models_fitted = purrr::map_int(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) 0L else length(models)
    }),
    fitted_models = purrr::map_chr(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        stringr::str_extract(names(models), "^m\\d+") |>
          paste(collapse = ", ")
      }
    })) |>
  rename(
    `Tidal feature` = constituent,
    `Observations` = n_obs,
    `Unique values` = n_unique,
    `Models fitted` = temporal_models_fitted,
    `Number fitted` = n_models_fitted,
    `Fitted model set` = fitted_models
  )

model_fit_status |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c", "l"),
    caption = "Temporal model fitting summary"
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    full_width = TRUE,
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  ) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(1, width = "110px") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2:5, width = "100px") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(6, width = "300px") |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "500px", fixed_thead = TRUE)

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {

    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))

            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

title: Temporal modelling for DublinPort
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at DublinPort.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for DublinPort
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

        error = function(e) {

            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
