title: Temporal modelling for EnniscronePier
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at EnniscronePier.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for EnniscronePier
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

## Show what was fitted

  transmute(constituent, n_obs, n_unique,
    temporal_models_fitted = purrr::map_lgl(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      !is.null(models) && length(models) > 0
    }),
    n_models_fitted = purrr::map_int(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) 0L else length(models)
    }),
    fitted_models = purrr::map_chr(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]

        NA_character_
      } else {
        stringr::str_extract(names(models), "^m\\d+") |>
          paste(collapse = ", ")

    })) |>

    `Tidal feature` = constituent,
    `Observations` = n_obs,

    `Number fitted` = n_models_fitted,

title: Temporal modelling for Foynes
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at Foynes.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)

title: Temporal modelling for Foynes
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

## Show what was fitted
## Show what was fitted
model_fit_status <- temporal_data_check |>
  transmute(constituent, n_obs, n_unique,
    temporal_models_fitted = purrr::map_lgl(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      !is.null(models) && length(models) > 0
    }),
    n_models_fitted = purrr::map_int(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) 0L else length(models)
    }),
    fitted_models = purrr::map_chr(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        stringr::str_extract(names(models), "^m\\d+") |>
          paste(collapse = ", ")
      }
    })) |>
  rename(
    `Tidal feature` = constituent,
    `Observations` = n_obs,
    `Unique values` = n_unique,
    `Models fitted` = temporal_models_fitted,
    `Number fitted` = n_models_fitted,
    `Fitted model set` = fitted_models
  )

model_fit_status |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c", "l"),
    caption = "Temporal model fitting summary"
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    full_width = TRUE,
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  ) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(1, width = "110px") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2:5, width = "100px") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(6, width = "300px") |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "500px", fixed_thead = TRUE)

title: Temporal modelling for Inishmore
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at Inishmore.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.

## Packages
library(arrow)

library(patchwork)

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"

da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>

## Split by constituent and create a list

    split(~constituent)

title: Temporal modelling for Inishmore
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

## Show what was fitted
## Show what was fitted
model_fit_status <- temporal_data_check |>
  transmute(constituent, n_obs, n_unique,
    temporal_models_fitted = purrr::map_lgl(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      !is.null(models) && length(models) > 0
    }),
    n_models_fitted = purrr::map_int(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) 0L else length(models)
    }),
    fitted_models = purrr::map_chr(constituent, \(const) {
      models <- res[[const]]
      if (is.null(models) || length(models) == 0) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        stringr::str_extract(names(models), "^m\\d+") |>
          paste(collapse = ", ")
      }
    })) |>
  rename(
    `Tidal feature` = constituent,
    `Observations` = n_obs,
    `Unique values` = n_unique,
    `Models fitted` = temporal_models_fitted,
    `Number fitted` = n_models_fitted,
    `Fitted model set` = fitted_models
  )

model_fit_status |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c", "l"),
    caption = "Temporal model fitting summary"
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    full_width = TRUE,
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  ) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(1, width = "110px") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2:5, width = "100px") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(6, width = "300px") |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "500px", fixed_thead = TRUE)

title: Temporal modelling for LimerickDock
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at LimerickDock.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for LimerickDock
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(

title: Temporal modelling for MercyHospital
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at MercyHospital.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for MercyHospital
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.

    ## Return result

## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

title: Temporal modelling for RossaveelPier
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at RossaveelPier.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for RossaveelPier
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {
            form_use <- form[!names(form) %in% c("m5_int_iid_ar1", "m6_int_iid_rw1", "m11_trend_iid_ar1", "m12_trend_iid_rw1")]

            message(sprintf(paste0("%s | %s has %i observations: ", "using reduced temporal model set."), params$station, const, n_obs))
        } else {
            form_use <- form
        }
        
        ## Report which models will be fitted
        message(sprintf("%s | %s: fitting %i temporal models: %s", params$station, const, length(form_use), paste(names(form_use), collapse = ", ")))
        
        ## Create model storage for this tidal level
        res[[const]] <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(form_use))
        names(res[[const]]) <- names(form_use)

        ## Fit temporal models
        for (j in seq_along(form_use)) {
            model_name <- names(form_use)[j]

            message(sprintf(paste0("========== Running model for %s: %s ", "| n = %i =========="), const, model_name, n_obs))
            
            ## Detailed diagnostics printed to terminal
            cat("\n\n",
                "============================================================\n",
                "STATION:     ", params$station, "\n",
                "CONSTITUENT: ", const, "\n",
                "MODEL:       ", model_name, "\n",
                "FORMULA:     ",
                paste(deparse(form_use[[j]]), collapse = " "),
                "\n",
                "N OBS:       ", n_obs, "\n",
                "N UNIQUE:    ", n_unique, "\n",
                "============================================================\n\n",
                sep = ""
            )

            flush.console()

            ## Try progressively more conservative INLA optimisation
            fit_attempt <- fit_inla_robust(
                formula = form_use[[j]],
                data = dc,
                control_compute = cc,
                station = params$station,
                constituent = const,
                model_name = model_name)

            
            ## Store result
            res[[const]][j] <- list(fit_attempt)
        }
        
        ## Identify models that failed
        model_ok <- !purrr::map_lgl(res[[const]], is.null)

        if (any(!model_ok)) {
            message(sprintf("%s | %s: %i of %i attempted temporal models failed.", params$station, const, sum(!model_ok), length(model_ok)))

            message(paste("Failed models:", paste(names(res[[const]])[!model_ok],collapse = ", ")))
        }

        ## Keep only successfully fitted models
        res[[const]] <- res[[const]][model_ok]

        ## If absolutely every attempted model failed, preserve a named NULL constituent so the results page knows that no models are available.
        if (length(res[[const]]) == 0) {
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
        }
    }

    ## Save models after all constituents have been processed
    saveRDS(res, fl)

} else {
    res <- readRDS(fl)
}

title: Temporal modelling for ShannonAirport
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at ShannonAirport.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for ShannonAirport
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.


Code
## Define formulas
form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS <- 5

## Also require at least three distinct values. This prevents temporal models
## being fitted to a series that is effectively constant.
MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES <- 3

## Threshold for using the full model set
## For short temporal series, models containing two simultaneous random effects
## can be weakly identified and numerically unstable.
## When fewer than 15 observations are available, omit:
##
##   m5  = intercept + iid + ar1
##   m6  = intercept + iid + rw1
##   m11 = trend + iid + ar1
##   m12 = trend + iid + rw1
MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET <- 15

## Summarise the amount of information available for each tidal level
temporal_data_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(db, \(dc, const) {
       values <- dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)]

        tibble(constituent = const, n_obs = length(values), n_unique = dplyr::n_distinct(values),
            value_sd = ifelse( length(values) > 1,  sd(values),NA_real_ ),
            fit_temporal_model = length(values) >= MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS & dplyr::n_distinct(values) >= MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES)
    }
)

## Create storage object
## Each constituent initially contains NULL. Models are added only when enough
## temporal observations are available.
res <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(const_levels))
names(res) <- const_levels

## INLA settings
cc <- list(cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE)

## Robust INLA fitting function
## Short temporal series can occasionally cause the Newton-Raphson optimiser
## to fail. Try increasingly conservative optimisation settings before giving
## up on an individual model.

fit_inla_robust <- function(formula, data, control_compute, station, constituent, model_name) {
    ## Attempt 1: normal fit using one thread
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 2: smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.25, restart = 2)),
        error = function(e) {
            NULL
        }
    )

    if (!is.null(fit)) {
        return(fit)
    }

    ## Attempt 3: even smaller Newton-Raphson steps
    fit <- tryCatch(
        inla(formula = formula, family = "gaussian", data = data, control.compute = control_compute, num.threads = 1,
            control.inla = list(step.factor = 0.10, restart = 3)),

        error = function(e) {
              NULL
        }
    )

    ## Return result
    ## If all three attempts failed this will return NULL.
    if (is.null(fit)) {
        message(sprintf(paste0("All fitting attempts failed for %s | %s | %s. ", "This model will be excluded."),station, constituent, model_name))
    }
    fit
}

## Saved model file
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("tide-models-%s-all-lat-hat.rds", params$station))

## Fit models
if (!file.exists(fl)) {
    for (const in const_levels) {
        ## Data for this tidal level
        dc <- db[[const]]
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(dc$value))
        n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(dc$value[!is.na(dc$value)])

        ## Check whether enough temporal information is available
        if (n_obs < MIN_TEMPORAL_OBS || n_unique < MIN_UNIQUE_VALUES) {
            message(sprintf(paste0("Skipping temporal models for %s at %s: ", "%i non-missing observations and %i unique values."), const, params$station, n_obs, n_unique))

            ## Preserve constituent name but record that no models were fitted
            res[const] <- list(NULL)
            next
        }

        ## Choose model set according to number of observations
        ## Short series: remove models containing two simultaneous random effects.
        ## Longer series: retain the full set of 12 models.

        if (n_obs < MIN_OBS_FULL_MODEL_SET) {

title: Temporal modelling for StPatricksQuayEast
text:
This page presents the temporal modelling of tidal characteristics at StPatricksQuayEast.
The analysis uses tidal features estimated from three-year rolling windows, including Highest Astronomical Tide (HAT), Mean High Water Springs (MHWS), Mean High Water Neaps (MHWN), Mean Sea Level (MSL), Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN), Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS), and Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).
A series of Bayesian temporal models are fitted using INLA to investigate how these tidal characteristics vary through time. The models consider different combinations of long-term temporal trends, unstructured year-to-year variation, and structured temporal dependence.
Model fit and predictive performance are compared to identify the temporal structure that best represents each tidal feature at the station.


Code
## Packages
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(TideHarmonics)
library(INLA)
here::i_am("index.qmd")
source(here::here("scripts", "_functions.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

## Full dataset
fl <- here::here("rds", sprintf("features-%s.rds", params$station))
da <- readRDS(fl)

## Set the levels for constituents
const_levels <- c("HAT","MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS","LAT")
## Select the windown interval
ws <- "y_3"
## Define years to predict
yrs <- range(da$year_mid) + c(-10, 10)
yrs_seq <- seq(yrs[1], yrs[2])

## Before splitting, rearrange and remove columns. ALSO, filter for window size
da <- da |>
    filter(window_size == ws) |>
    select(year_start, year_mid, year_end, constituent, value, st_id, lat, lon)

## Split by constituent and create a list
db <- da |>
    split(~constituent)

## Arrange and complete with more years
db <- imap(db, \(x, nm) {
    x |>
        arrange(year_mid) |>
        complete(year_mid = yrs_seq,
            fill = list(
                constituent = nm,
                st_id = unique(x$st_id)[1],
                lat = unique(x$lat)[1],
                lon = unique(x$lon)[1]
            )) |>
        mutate(constituent = fct_relevel(constituent, const_levels),
            id = seq_along(year_mid), id2 = id, id3 = id)
})

title: Temporal modelling for StPatricksQuayEast
text:
Model fitting checks and safeguards
Before fitting the temporal models, the amount of information available for each tidal feature is assessed. Temporal models are fitted only when a feature has at least five non-missing rolling-window estimates and at least three distinct observed values. These checks prevent temporal models from being fitted to extremely short series or to series that are effectively constant and so contain insufficient information to estimate temporal structure.
The complexity of the candidate model set is also adjusted according to the length of the available time series. When fewer than 15 non-missing temporal observations are available, models containing two simultaneous random-effect components are omitted. Specifically, the following models are excluded for shorter series:

m5: intercept + IID + AR(1)
m6: intercept + IID + RW1
m11: trend + IID + AR(1)
m12: trend + IID + RW1

These models contain both an unstructured IID component and a structured temporal component. When few observations are available, these can be difficult to identify and the models can become unstable. Shorter series are fitted using the reduced set of eight candidate models, while series containing at least 15 observations are fitted using the full set of twelve models.
The models are fitted using INLA with Gaussian observation errors. Because some of the temporal series are short and some of the more flexible models can be numerically challenging, a fitting procedure is used to ensure models are fitted successfully wherever possible. Each model is initially fitted using the standard INLA optimisation settings. If this attempt fails, the model is refitted using progressively smaller Newton–Raphson step sizes and additional optimiser restarts. A model is excluded only if all three fitting attempts fail.
If none of the candidate models can be fitted successfully, the feature is recorded as having no available temporal model rather than terminating the analysis for the entire station.
The final model-fit summary records, for each tidal feature, the number of temporal observations and unique values available, whether temporal modelling was possible, the number of models successfully fitted, and the specific candidate models retained for subsequent comparison.

form <- gen_model_formulas()
form_levels <- names(form)

## Minimum amount of temporal information required
## A station/constituent must have at least this many non-missing rolling-window
## estimates before the temporal INLA models are fitted.
